title: The streams close
hookLine: orders, schools, communities, places and music
tomorrow: Names of God in the Granth

lines: ONE CHANNEL LOOKS LIKE THE RIVER.
cards: From high on a hill, a river delta doesn't look like one river. It looks like a hand of silver fingers, braiding apart and back together on the way to the sea.
Stand on the bank of any one channel and you'd swear it was the only one. Go up the hill and you see the whole shape. This block has been a walk along the channels of the Sikh panth.
Today is the view from the hill, before the path turns to Sikh thought.

teach.b: Here's the shape. First, the orders: Udasis in renunciation, Nirmalas in learning, Sevapanthis in service, and the Nihang dals in blue.
Then the schools: the Damdami Taksal and its careful pronunciation, the Akhand Kirtani Jatha and its nights of kirtan, the Nanaksar tradition.

Then the communities: Namdharis in white, Baba Dayal's Nirankaris, Sikh Dharma in the West, Sindhi devotees of Nanak, Sikligar, Lubana and Vanjara Sikhs, the Sikhs of Assam, Mazhabi Sikhs, craftsmen and builders, and the Ravidassia community with its own story.

Then the places: the Harmandir's day and the Akal Takht, Delhi's gurdwaras, Nankana and Kartarpur, Panja Sahib, Anandpur, Fatehgarh, Muktsar, Goindval, Khadur, Tarn Taran, Baba Bakala, Kiratpur, snowy Hemkunt, and gurdwaras abroad.

Then the music and the arts: rababis, ragas and simple tunes, dhadis, kavishri, katha, gurmat sangeet, painting, architecture, phulkari. And last, the studies, the open questions, and one Granth at the center of them all.
Guru Nanak has an image for streams.
In the Japji, on Ang 5, he says, here in paraphrase, that rivers and streams flow into the ocean, yet cannot know how vast it is.
The streams of the panth are like that. Each pours into something larger than itself, and none of them holds all of it. That's a fitting place to turn from the people of the panth to its thought.
Tomorrow the path begins with the names of God in the Granth.

how: The Sikh panth lives in many streams, including orders, schools, communities, historic places and musical traditions, and Sikhs visit gurdwaras and gatherings beyond their own, with the Guru Granth Sahib at the center of the Sikh streams.

o: a look back at all the panth's streams
a ruling that ended debate between groups
the day the Sikh orders were dissolved

games.q: inside the streams close: tap the pairs.

s: one stream of the panth holds all of it
like rivers in the Japji's ocean, none holds all of it.
in the Japji, streams flow into the ocean without knowing how vast it is
this block covered only orders and schools
it covered orders, schools, communities, places, music, art and open questions.

games.q: you're Guru Nanak, describing how small anyone's praise is beside God's greatness. what image do you use?
o: rivers and streams flowing into the ocean, unable to know its size.
a mountain no one can climb.
games.why: on Ang 5 of the Japji, rivers and streams pour into the ocean and still cannot know how vast it is.

practice: Let the list pass through your mind once more without hurrying, an order, a school, a community, a place, a kind of music, and notice which one catches.
Name it to yourself plainly, maybe a gurdwara you could reach or a kirtan you've never heard live, and if you pray, offer that wish to Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: The streams close. Orders, schools, communities, places and music: the living streams of the panth, none of them holding all of it. Today's word.
